source_evidence.observation: F is a symmetric set of finite base-beta, precision-p floating-point numbers containing zero; fl rounds to nearest with arbitrary tie-breaking, and u = (1/2) beta^(1-p) is the unit roundoff. Underflow and overflow are excluded where stated.

source_evidence.anchor: Final paragraph before section 4.1, diag convention
source_evidence.observation: diag(f(i)) denotes the n-by-n diagonal matrix with diagonal entry f(i), with the index i implicitly ranging from 1 through n.

For A in F^(m-by-n), m >= n, completed Gaussian elimination without underflow or overflow produces L_hat in F^(m-by-n) and U_hat in F^(n-by-n) such that L_hat U_hat = A + Delta A and |Delta A| <= n u |L_hat||U_hat|. If m = n, the sharper bounds are |Delta A| <= diag((i-1)u)|L_hat||U_hat| <= (n-1)u|L_hat||U_hat|.

The proof analyzes Doolittle's mathematically equivalent formulation. At step k, upper-factor residuals have coefficient (k-1)u and lower-factor residuals have coefficient ku, independently of summation order.

source_evidence.anchor: Final coefficient comparison in the proof of Theorem 4.2
source_evidence.observation: The rectangular coefficient follows from k <= n. In the square case, an entry below the diagonal has k < i, hence ku <= (i-1)u <= (n-1)u; together with the upper-factor coefficient this yields the rowwise and uniform bounds.
The improved constants are exact multiples of u, contain no quadratic-in-u remainder, and impose no dimension condition analogous to nu < 1.

binders: Inherited floating-point context: beta >= 2 and p >= 1 determine a finite floating-point set F and unit roundoff u = (1/2) beta^(1-p). [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Sections 2.1-2.2]

Let m and n be matrix dimensions with m >= n, and let A belong to F^(m-by-n). Positivity and integrality of the dimensions are implicit in the matrix notation and the loop k = 1,...,n. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Theorem 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed 694), Doolittle formulas]

definitions_and_conventions: F consists of finite floating-point numbers in base beta and precision p, with a finite exponent range; it is symmetric and contains zero. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Section 2.1]
fl is round-to-nearest with no prescribed tie-breaking rule, and u = (1/2) beta^(1-p), so u <= 1/2. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), equations (2.1a)-(2.1b)]
diag((i-1)u) is the n-by-n diagonal matrix whose ith diagonal entry is (i-1)u, with i = 1,...,n. [PDF p. 9 (printed 692), diag convention; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), equation (4.2)]

Hats distinguish computed floating-point factors from exact input data; the displayed factor product and residual identity are mathematical equalities formed from those computed values. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Theorem 4.2]
implicit_context: The theorem's quantifier order is: choose admissible dimensions and A; run a completing Gaussian-elimination computation under the stated arithmetic exclusions; obtain L_hat and U_hat; then define or assert Delta A and its bounds. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Theorem 4.2]

The standard reading of |Delta A|, |L_hat|, and |U_hat| is entrywise absolute value, with matrix inequalities interpreted componentwise and |L_hat||U_hat| denoting ordinary matrix multiplication of the absolute-value matrices; the inspected pages do not separately define this notation. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Theorem 4.2 and equation (4.2)]

statement.algorithm_linkage: The section announces any variant of Gaussian elimination, while the proof uses Doolittle's method as one mathematically equivalent formulation. For k = 1,...,n it computes y_kj = a_kj - sum_(r=1)^(k-1) l_hat_kr u_hat_rj for j = k,...,n and y_ik = (a_ik - sum_(r=1)^(k-1) l_hat_ir u_hat_rk)/u_hat_kk for i = k+1,...,m, takes their computed values as u_hat_kj and l_hat_ik, and sets l_hat_kk = 1. Lemma 4.1 then gives the local residual bounds (4.3a)-(4.3b) for whatever order of evaluation. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Section 4.2; PDF p. 11 (printed 694), Doolittle formulas and equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]

error_notions: Delta A is a backward error on the input matrix: the computed factors exactly factor A + Delta A. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Theorem 4.2]
The error is bounded componentwise relative to the magnitude product |L_hat||U_hat|, rather than relative to |A| or by a normwise condition. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Theorem 4.2 and equation (4.2)]
For square matrices, the first sharper estimate is row-dependent: row i is scaled by (i-1)u. [PDF p. 9 (printed 692), diag convention; PDF p. 10 (printed 693), equation (4.2)]

Locally, equation (4.3a) uses (k-1)u for j = k,...,n, whereas equation (4.3b) uses k u for i = k+1,...,m. [PDF p. 11 (printed 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]

The paper explicitly presents these improved constants as O(u^2)-free and unconditional, without a restriction such as n u < 1. [PDF p. 4 (printed 687), discussion following equation (1.8)]

Underflow is defined as an inexact rounding of a real number lying in the subnormal range; floating-point addition cannot underflow under this definition, while multiplication and division can. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Section 2.1]
F contains only finite floating-point numbers, and overflow to infinity is outside the admitted execution. [PDF p. 5 (printed 688), Section 2.1]

The factorization relation is L_hat U_hat = A + Delta A, so the sign convention is Delta A = L_hat U_hat - A. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Theorem 4.2]

contract_plain_english: For any finite floating-point matrix A with m rows and n columns, m >= n, run a completing Gaussian-elimination variant in round-to-nearest arithmetic without underflow or overflow. Its computed m-by-n lower factor L_hat and n-by-n upper factor U_hat exactly factor a perturbed matrix A + Delta A, where the componentwise residual is at most n u times |L_hat||U_hat|. When A is square, row i has the sharper coefficient (i-1)u, yielding the uniform coefficient (n-1)u. These constants are exact, contain no O(u^2) term, impose no condition such as n u < 1, and arise from the Doolittle local coefficients (k-1)u and k u. [PDF p. 10 (printed 693), Theorem 4.2 and equation (4.2); PDF p. 11 (printed 694), equations (4.3a)-(4.3b) and final coefficient comparison]
